findings.claim: The unavailable delivery-cadence documentation omits the required carried-payload marker `one referenced asset is absent`.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 1.2 requires rewriting SKILL.md/profile.md to declare the capability unavailable with the exact carried-payload markers `UNAVAILABLE IN THIS PROJECT`; `one referenced asset is absent` where a reference must remain; the added SKILL.md line contains `UNAVAILABLE IN THIS PROJECT` but not `one referenced asset is absent`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the required carried-payload marker or provide the remaining asset reference in the documented form expected by the carried-payload contract.

findings.claim: The adaptation record's changedDocumentation list omits the dist payload documentation copies changed by this diff.
findings.evidence: The adaptation record lists only `skills/delivery-cadence/SKILL.md` and `skills/delivery-cadence/references/profile.md`, while the diff also changes `dist/plugins/claude/prometheus-skills-mini/skills/delivery-cadence/SKILL.md`, `dist/plugins/claude/prometheus-skills-mini/skills/delivery-cadence/references/profile.md`, `dist/plugins/codex/prometheus-skills-mini/skills/delivery-cadence/SKILL.md`, and `dist/plugins/codex/prometheus-skills-mini/skills/delivery-cadence/references/profile.md`; acceptance requires the record to name changed documentation and final hashes auditable by a reviewer.
findings.suggested_fix: Either include the changed dist documentation paths in the provenance record or clarify the field is source-only and add a separate field for regenerated payload documentation.

findings.claim: The secret scanner misclassifies duplicate JSON key/value digests because it matches parsed subjects to the first unused line with the same digest rather than the subject's actual source location.
findings.evidence: `scanText` builds line candidates by digest only, then `walkJson` uses `candidates.find((entry) => !entry.used && entry.digest === digest)` to assign a line to each parsed key/value hit; with duplicate credential-shaped substrings in multiple JSON locations, a parsed hit can consume a different location's line, making location-bound dispositions unreliable.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a JSON parser that preserves token locations, or treat parsed key/value hits without line binding and use pointer+digest for structured location matching.

findings.claim: The provider-token detector only recognizes `sk-` tokens and can miss other provider keys despite the criterion requiring provider keys generally.
findings.evidence: Acceptance and constraint text describe no inline database credentials or provider keys; `DETECTORS` contains only `/--(user|pass)=/g` and `/sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g`, so common provider key shapes not beginning with `sk-` are not detected.
findings.suggested_fix: Either constrain the spec to the exact intended token family or add detector patterns for all provider-key formats covered by the security boundary.
